title: Provenance block
description: The honesty fields every acquisition-family payload carries so a consumer can tell a complete answer from a truncated one and a fresh body from a cached one. This is the machine-readable form of the repo's house rule that an absent or partial upstream value is never rendered as a plausible number, and that a derived body must say so. Field sources: backend/data/internal/research/cryptorank/types.go CrEnvelope (upstream, fetchedAt, cache, count, upstreamTotal, slice, changeSource), news Envelope (upstream, timestamp), khala Envelope (upstream, fetchedAt, cache, count, upstreamTotal, slice, missingSlugs), llama Envelope (upstream, fetchedAt, upstreamTotal, derived).

upstream.description: The exact upstream URL (or route) this body came from, as the envelopes already report it.

received_at.description: Null while no carrier exists (see time.json#/$defs/received_at); a consumer MUST NOT substitute `fetched_at` for it.

cache.description: Cache disposition of THIS response, as the sidecar already reports it: 'MISS' on a live fetch, 'HIT' on a cache read.

derived.description: Non-null whenever the body was transformed (sorted, trimmed, aggregated). Names the transform, so a client never implies the body is upstream-verbatim. Precedent: llama's `derived: 'sorted by tvl (upstream sends unsorted)'`.

count.description: How many rows THIS body contains.

total.description: How many rows the source had. count < total means truncated, and a client must render '50 of 8386', never '50 rows exist'.

slice.description: Human-readable statement of the truncation, when one happened.

missing.description: Identifiers the parse expected and could not find (khala's missingSlugs) - a loud partial, reported rather than hidden.
